_comment: Golden metric-row vectors. ONE dataset judged by both sides of the historisation boundary: colca-historian (Go) decides which column a measurement lands in, and whatever serves history reads that column back out. They are separate implementations in separate languages, so the mapping between a _Metric value and its storage column is exactly the kind of fact that drifts silently — a value written to value_number and read from value_text simply disappears from a chart. The cases RESTATE shipped behaviour (internal/historian/record.go); changing one is a storage-format change and needs every reader updated.

cases.why: a string parameter keeps its text column
a status flag is boolean, never the number 1
an array is a structure too
beyond float64 precision the digits are kept verbatim rather than rounded into value_number

not_measurements.why: a tombstone deletes the retained value; it is not a reading
a null value has no column to land in

refused.why: without a signal the row is unattributable and nothing downstream can repair it

timestamps._comment: Pins the wire unit for Metric.timestamp: unix seconds, float, fractional part allowed (franzmq's default `datetime.now(UTC).timestamp()`; connector/src/reader.py and dataops/src/dataops/outputs.py agree). Only colca-historian (Go) decodes this field from the wire, so these vectors are judged by vectors_test.go alone -- the Python suite reads timestamps back out of Postgres, already decoded, and never re-parses the wire value.

cases.why: the wire timestamp is unix seconds; the fractional part is sub-second precision, not milliseconds

without a payload timestamp the row falls back to the store's own ingest clock, which stays epoch-MILLISECONDS -- that value comes from colca's store (store_ts_ms above), never from the wire, so it keeps its own unit
